lessons: Lead hooks with bold, counter-intuitive facts or striking comparisons rather than restating the title or topic (e.g., Greenland shark video reached 1.85x retention at 10% with 'older than the United States').

Avoid repeating the video title or hook idea immediately after the start; repeating questions causes major drop-offs (e.g., Potato sprouted drop of 31.9% and Garlic drop of 34.0% right after the intro).
Eliminate generic filler and obvious observations; viewers leave when given redundant fluff (e.g., 'They look like similar fruits' lost 30.0%, 'They are not just there to look cool' lost 31.5%).

Do not pause narration for artificial engagement prompts like 'Pause and guess'; interactive pauses cause measurable audience drop (e.g., Foil video dropped 15.2% during 'Pause and guess... three, two, one').

Maintain continuous narrative momentum with high-density scientific detail to drive end-to-end retention above platform benchmarks (e.g., Tuna vs Cod achieved 0.86 vs_similar_end and Webb telescope achieved 0.65 vs_similar_end).
worst_moment_types: Immediate repetition of the title or initial hook concept in the following sentence.
Generic filler phrases and restatements of the obvious (e.g., 'They look like similar fruits').
Interactive callouts or artificial countdown pauses (e.g., 'Pause and guess... three, two, one').
Duplicate script audio lines played back-to-back.
best_hook_types: Historical or scale-based provocative facts (e.g., 'This shark is older than the United States').
Direct sensory/visual contrast comparisons (e.g., 'Tuna steak looks like deep red beef, while a cod fillet is bright white').
Challenging established common knowledge directly in sentence one (e.g., 'Pluto seemed like our solar system's edge, yet astronomers...').
